title: Amend the charter, or accept 130 stories as 1.0
description:
DEFERRED DECISION - raised 2026-08-22, user chose to decide AFTER ITER-0000 ships.

The charter-grounded cut removed 19 of 149 stories, leaving 130 scheduled. Only a 12% cut; 130 is still a very large 1.0. The charter does not authorize a deeper cut - going further means AMENDING docs/charter-1.0.md.

ADDED BY THE OPUS GATE - two asymmetries the charter itself cannot resolve, fold into this decision:
1. ITER-0010's 17 water/sewage/heating stories have NO row in the Ships-in-1.0 table at all, yet charter:110 defers 'treatment tiers'. STORY-0127 (water piped with a quality grade) and STORY-0132 (sewage treat-or-discharge) were KEPT on the judgement that a single treatment step with one quality ceiling is not 'tiers'. Defensible, but the charter is silent, not supportive.
2. STORY-0023 (cross-border electricity trade via import/export transformers) stays while STORY-0019 was deferred on charter:110 'grid depth (transformers...)'. Different device - border endpoint vs voltage step-down - and the charter names electricity trade in neither list. Deliberate asymmetry, flagged so it is not mistaken for an oversight.

When ITER-0000 ships, revisit with actual cost data, then decide whether Ships-in-1.0 rows move to Post-1.0.

TRAP: user has twice chosen completeness over leanness. Lead with a recommendation but expect the fuller option to win.

title: Dispatches wedge: bakeries have no trucks but every bread purchase creates one
description:
Three unbounded-wait dispatch states, none with a timeout or cancellation. The dispatches Vec grows without bound and is walked every tick.

(c) IS THE GAMEPLAY-BREAKING ONE: every human bread purchase now creates a Dispatch, but bakeries are kind="store" (base_mod/companies.lua:11,126) and goods_company.rs:129 spawns trucks ONLY `if ckind == CompanyKind::Factory`. VERIFIED. So a city's bakeries accumulate one permanently-reserved dispatch per unfilled meal. Worse: recipe_should_produce reads RAW capital, not capital-reserved, so the bakery also stops producing while holding stock it can never sell.

(a) Loading with no route to buyer (market.rs:520-537): door_pos(buyer) returns None once the buyer's building is demolished; ticks_left is already 0 so it retries forever. The seller was ALREADY debited at ToSource arrival - quantity permanently destroyed. The truck is never dispatcher.free'd (only happens at market.rs:557), so it leaks too.

(b) ToSource with truck: Some(v) where the vehicle entity is gone: world.vehicles.get(v) -> None -> .unwrap_or(false) (market.rs:494-499) -> never arrives. reserved[seller] frozen forever.

FIX: needs a cancellation/timeout path. Consider also whether stores should get trucks, or whether human purchases should create dispatches at all.

And it is single-shot: SDD:16 'Do not pause to check in with your human partner between tasks', SDD:19 'A running plan does not wait on a human', with exactly four stop conditions (irreversible / security / out-of-worktree side effect / plan unsalvageable) — none is 'the work looks wrong'. RELEASE-NOTES:19 shows this was deliberately loosened this release. So it stops the wrong DESIGN, not 130 stories of drift. | CLAIM 3 writing-plans scale = CONFIRMED structurally. git log: only 3 commits ever on writing-plans/SKILL.md (2x 2026-07-05 prose trims, +3 lines on 2026-08-12 adding a 'Spec:' pointer) — substantively unchanged since iterative-development was written, so the criticism is current. No numeric ceiling anywhere; the only scale handling is advisory prose (SKILL.md:20-24 'suggest breaking this into separate plans'), keyed on 'independent subsystems' — so 130 stories in one non-decomposable domain trips no rule. Concrete breaks at scale: (a) No-Placeholders rule forbids compression, so the plan is ONE file with full code for all 130 tasks; (b) spec coverage is a manual skim the plan's own author runs on itself (:150 'not a subagent dispatch') = 370x130 from memory; (c) SDD's mandatory pre-flight conflict scan is pairwise, 'One row for every pair of tasks that share a file or an interface' (SDD:170) = up to 8385 rows before Task 1; (d) controller reads the whole plan into context (SDD:161) while conceding it will be compacted (SDD:139). 'Loses the plot' as behavior = unverified, I did not run it. | CLAIM 4 documents never verified against code = CONFIRMED. Spec self-review (brainstorming:207-218) and plan self-review (writing-plans:148-158) are document-internal / doc-vs-doc only. Both dispatchable document-reviewer templates (brainstorming/spec-document-reviewer-prompt.md, writing-plans/plan-document-reviewer-prompt.md) are ORPHANS at this SHA — grep shows refs only from RELEASE-NOTES and the 2026-01-22 plan/spec that created them, no SKILL.md calls either — and even they only read the spec/plan paths, never code. The one doc<->code check is the SDD task reviewer, which runs the OTHER way (code conforms to brief) and is barred from the codebase; unverifiable requirements become an unresolved warning item. No hook, no script, no pre-commit does it (.pre-commit-config.yaml targets evals/, which .gitignore:13 deliberately excludes as a separate repo and which is absent). Exception worth naming: writing-skills DOES empirically validate, via RED/GREEN pressure scenarios against subagent BEHAVIOR — never against code. | Q-A three SDD scripts: sdd-workspace = mkdir + self-ignoring .gitignore + print abs path (plan-scoped because a stale ledger made controllers re-dispatch whole task sequences); task-brief = 9-line awk with a fence guard and a ([^0-9]|$) guard so Task 1 doesn't match Task 10, extracts one task to a file — but does NOT carry Global Constraints, which the controller must hand-copy verbatim into both dispatches; review-package = git log --oneline + diff --stat + diff -U10 over BASE..HEAD into one uniquely named file (BASE not HEAD~1, repeated 3x, because HEAD~1 silently drops all but the last commit of a multi-commit task). All three exist to keep artifacts OUT of the controller's context. Key finding: review VERDICTS are never captured in a file — they return as the subagent's final message into controller context, and the only durable trace is a ledger line the controller chooses to write; then rm -rf destroys the ledger, leaving the 'Rulings I made' roll-up in the final message as the sole channel to the human. | Q-B three-path router: introduced by THIS commit (+117/-14 on brainstorming/SKILL.md; the phrase appears only in the commit subject, nowhere in the tree). Replaces a single-path flow. Classify BEFORE the first question and say it out loud: Spike (feasibility question, output is an answer not code, nod suffices, artifacts labeled throwaway) / Bounded (change to a flow that ALREADY EXISTS in this repo — 'bounded measures the repo, not your familiarity', so every greenfield routes architectural — short design in chat, no spec, no plan doc) / Architectural (new projects/subsystems/interface changes — full questions to approaches to sectioned design to spec to writing-plans). One-way ratchet: in doubt take the heavier path, hidden complexity upgrades mid-task, nothing downgrades. It routes CEREMONY, not approval — all three paths end at the same 'Human approves?' diamond, and the HARD-GATE was rewritten this release to say so. Classification is self-declared, unenforced, unrecorded. | Full report: /tmp/fw-study/reports/sp-adversary.md | side effects: this comment only.

title: Ext-trade surplus sale double-spends reserved stock
description:
LEDGER BROKEN. Units created from nothing during ordinary gameplay.

market.rs:398-410 (ext-trade surplus loop) reads `capital` and NEVER reads `reserved`. `reserved` is read in exactly ONE place in the crate: the domestic filter_map at market.rs:319-322.

SUBTLETY - the domestic loop is NOT the bug. It decrements sorder.qty as it reserves, so within ONE make_trades pass the ext block sees order.qty == capital - reserved and closes correctly. The hole is `sell_all` (market.rs:191): it re-posts the order at FULL capital and forgets the reservation. recipe_act calls it every production cycle (goods_company.rs:56-61), so the overwrite is routine.

BREAK WINDOW: final capital = stock - reserved, negative iff reserved > stock. Production requires capital < amount*(mult+1) and reserved <= capital, so the window is amount*mult < capital < amount*(mult+1). EMPTY for amount=1. OPEN for amount=10.

REAL PROTOTYPE THAT HITS IT: base_mod/companies.lua flour-factory, production {{"flour",10}}, storage_multiplier=5 -> stock 50, gate capital<60, window 50<capital<60. VERIFIED present.

Sequence: F capital 59, domestic matches 55 (reserved=55, sorder.qty=4, capital still 59). recipe_act produces +10 -> 69, sell_all overwrites order to qty 69/stock 50. Next pass ext-trade: qty_sell = 69-50 = 19, guard passes, capital -> 50, 19 exported for real money. Trucks arrive, Loading debits 55 -> capital = -5. 69 units existed; 55 delivered + 19 exported = 74. FIVE CREATED FROM NOTHING.

Then capital<0 makes sell_all bail (c<=0), so the loss is silently absorbed as lost production.

FIX: guard and compute surplus against `*cap - reserved` / `order.qty.saturating_sub(reserved)`, or make sell_all post capital-reserved.

ALSO IN THIS BLOCK (separate, pre-existing): market.rs:387-396 credits the buyer BEFORE checking find_external. mod.rs:69-78 returns None when world.freight_stations is empty. So with no freight station - normal early game - every unmatched buy order is granted free every tick, no money debited, no Trade recorded so it does not even appear in EcoStats. Scarcity is off. FIX: move the credit inside the Some(ext) arm.
close_reason: commit fdfabca: ext-trade surplus computed against order.qty.saturating_sub(reserved) and guarded on *cap - reserved; buy-order credit moved inside the Some(ext) arm. Guard scenario_ledger_exttrade_double_spend seen FAILING first ('55 delivered + 19 exported > 69 ever produced, capital -5') then passing. 26 tests green.

title: No scenario asserts a conservation invariant
description:
The cheapest guard that would have caught BOTH sov-ledger-exttrade and sov-ledger-remove, per the ledger audit.

Today nothing in simulation/src/tests/scenarios/ asserts conservation. hoarding.rs scenarios 0082/0083/0151 assert point values of m.capital(...) for two hand-built souls; they never sum the ledger, never exercise Market::remove mid-dispatch, and never let the ext-trade surplus branch fire.

ADD: a per-item assertion that `sum(capital across all souls) + sum(in-flight dispatch qty)` is unchanged across any tick in which no produce() ran.

Then make it fail on purpose once (mutation) before trusting it.

title: Market::remove leaves reserved/requested/dispatches behind
description:
LEDGER BROKEN. Demolishing a building mid-delivery creates units and leaves a permanent phantom ledger row.

market.rs:195-202 Market::remove clears sell_orders, buy_orders, capital. It does NOT clear `reserved`, `requested`, or `dispatches`.

Callers are real gameplay paths: world.rs:112 (human dies), world.rs:157 (freight station), world.rs:178 (goods company). A company is killed as soon as its building is gone - goods_company.rs:187-190.

Sequence: F sells 10 flour to B, dispatch in ToSource, truck driving. Player demolishes F. remove() deletes capital[F]; dispatches and reserved[F] survive. Truck arrives -> market.rs:503 `*m.capital.entry(seller).or_default() -= qty` RESURRECTS an entry for the demolished company at -10. Truck reaches B -> market.rs:546 credits B +10.

B receives 10 flour from a building that no longer exists. The -10 phantom row is Serialized into every save and can never be reconciled because remove() already ran.

Same shape with roles swapped: demolish the BUYER mid-ToDestination and market.rs:546 resurrects it at +10.

FIX: remove() must also drop reserved/requested for the soul AND cancel every dispatch naming it, releasing the seller's reservation if it has not yet loaded.
close_reason: commit fdfabca: Market::remove now clears reserved/requested and retains only dispatches not naming the soul. Guard scenario_ledger_remove_leak seen FAILING first ('phantom row: Some(-10)') then passing. Truck-not-freed remainder scoped to sov-dispatch-wedge-ab4 with a ponytail: comment.

title: lsp-first-read-guard deadlocks workers with no LSP tool
description:
HARNESS, not game code. ~/.claude/hooks/lsp-first-read-guard.js blocks Read on code files until an LSP warmup call, but never checks whether the agent HAS the LSP tool. Subagents frequently do not: one implementer reported 'ToolSearch found no LSP tool at all, for any query' while the hook still blocked Read. The only remaining way to read a file is 'bash cat', which rules/tool-discipline.md forbids — there is no legal move.

Second defect: the state flag is ~/.claude/state/lsp-ready-<md5(cwd)>, keyed on cwd ONLY. agentId is not in the PreToolUse payload and all subagents share the session's sessionId, so concurrent workers in one repo share ONE read budget. Verified: agents a7257c13c1cd759f4 and ad87181ae55be8f94 (identical promptId d2aea593, same cwd, 27s apart) drew from one counter; one hit 'Gate 5 — Read #6 requires at least 2 LSP navigation calls' having made only one nav call itself.

Impact measured on session a4b9c11d: 4 of 15 workers hard-blocked, 7 mentioned the guard or missing LSP. NOBODY reported it as a blocker — they silently degraded to bash cat, so tool discipline was being violated wave-wide and invisibly.

TRAP: do not 'fix' this by keying the flag per-agent. The payload does not carry an agent id; it cannot be done.

FIX (written and tested, NOT installed — global user config needs Caio's go-ahead):
/tmp/claude-1000/-home-caio-soviet-simulator/a4b9c11d-b7b9-453d-a0ca-3d7e14efbd86/scratchpad/lsp-first-read-guard.patched.js
Adds a per-file consecutive-block counter; after 2 blocks on the same file it relents with a loud systemMessage instead of blocking forever, and a successful read clears that file's counter. An agent that actually calls LSP never reaches the hatch.

VERIFIED STANDALONE (fake HOME, clean state):
  deadlock case, same Read retried 4x -> exit 2, exit 2, exit 0 (RELENTED), exit 0
  regression, warmup done -> .md exit 0 | read#1 exit 0 | read#2 exit 0 | read#3 exit 0 + WARNING | read#4 exit 2 Gate 4 | re-read exit 0
  node --check passes
Normal gate semantics are unchanged; only repeated blocks on one file relent.
close_reason: Patch installed 2026-08-24 at ~/.claude/hooks/lsp-first-read-guard.js (backup: .bak-2026-08-24). Per-file consecutive-block counter, RELENT_AFTER=2, applied at gates 1/4/5, counter cleared on any successful read. Differential smoke test in a real git repo outside the /tmp allow-list, HOME isolated: PATCHED -> block,block,RELENT,RELENT ; ORIGINAL -> block,block,block,block (deadlock confirmed). node --check OK. NOTE: the cwd-keyed shared read budget is NOT fixed - the PreToolUse payload carries no agent id, so concurrent subagents still share one counter. The relent path makes that survivable rather than fatal.

title: The design pillars have no runtime assertions
description:
Both pillars were violated in shipped code and no test noticed.

"Nothing teleports" and "never game over" are stated in CLAUDE.md, encoded as prose in ACs, and enforced NOWHERE at runtime.

EVIDENCE: the ext-trade buy block credited a buyer their full requested quantity whenever find_external returned None - which it does whenever world.freight_stations is empty, the normal early game. Every unmatched buy order was granted free, every tick, unpaid, and absent from EcoStats. Scarcity, the entire pressure source of the design, was switched off. It compiled, passed review, and passed every test. Found only when a specialist agent traced conservation across the seam (commit fdfabca).

The conservation invariant in tests/scenarios/ledger.rs is the first assertion of a pillar in the codebase and it only covers quantity.

PROPOSAL: give each pillar a cheap standing assertion the sentinel corpus runs every iteration.
  - nothing teleports: no capital increases without either a completed dispatch unload or a declared production/import source. Generalises ledger.rs beyond a hand-built pair of souls.
  - never game over: no code path terminates a run or produces an unrecoverable state; unmet need must always degrade.
  - clearing by queue, never by price: no Money read gates a physical flow. Partly a grep, better as a runtime assertion.

Cheaper than it sounds and it catches the class of bug that survives code review because the code is correct - it is the DESIGN that is violated.

title: job-opening reserves stock but never releases it
description:
market.rs:334-336 reserves for EVERY match. market.rs:363 then skips dispatch creation for job-opening (`if kind != ItemID::new("job-opening")`). The dispatch is the ONLY thing that ever decrements `reserved` (market.rs:505) or debits capital (market.rs:503).

So for job-opening: acquire happens, release never does.

Sequence: company C does produce(job_opening, 5) then sell_all (goods_company.rs:166-167). Five humans each buy 1 (human.rs:269). Five matches -> reserved[C] = 5, sell order emptied, but capital[C][job-opening] stays at 5 forever instead of falling to 0.

CURRENTLY SILENT: no production reader of capital(soul, job_opening) outside tests.

LIVE TRAP: any future re-post of the job-opening sell order (rehiring after a worker dies) hits cap_seller - already_reserved = 5 - 5 = 0 < 1, and THE COMPANY CAN NEVER HIRE AGAIN.

FIX: release the reservation immediately for items that get no dispatch, or do not reserve on that branch.

BONUS - false comment: market.rs:358 claims a human buyer owns no building for a truck to route to. human.rs:272 calls set_owner(house, soul), so door_pos DOES resolve for humans. The conclusion (skip dispatch for job-opening) still stands on its other reason, but the stated premise is wrong and will mislead the next editor.
close_reason: commit fdfabca: job-opening debits at match time instead of reserving, since it never gets a dispatch and the dispatch is the only release path. Guard scenario_ledger_job_opening_reserve_leak seen FAILING first (left: 3, right: 0) then passing. Also fixed the false comment about human buyers owning no building (human.rs:272 set_owner).

title: Verify the 370 SUBSTRATE claims in the requirements corpus
description:
GATE on every remaining iteration. The largest known liability in the project, and nothing tracked it until now.

Every AC in requirements/EPIC-*.md carries a [SUBSTRATE: ...] tag asserting what the code already provides. Measured 2026-08-23:

  370 ACs carry a tag        103 cite an exact file:line
  265 ABSENT   33 CONFLICTS   26 PROVIDED   19 PARTIAL   17 UNAUDITED   10 OURS

NOT ONE HAS EVER BEEN VERIFIED. The extraction wrote them from spec prose. iterative-development's PAR reviews asked "what is missing?", never "is this true?". The format even has a tag literally named UNAUDITED.

WHY THIS IS P1: every serious failure of 2026-08-23 was a wrong substrate claim.
  - "extend map_dynamic::Dispatcher" - truck registration was commented out; the dispatcher had never seen a truck. The agent built the mechanism the AC forbade.
  - "copy the freight_station train pattern" - trains have no parking layer; trucks only move when Driving with a Transporter collider. Premise false.
  - base_mod/items.lua sets optout_exttrade on 1 item of 21. That line falsified three claims in a landed commit.
Each cost 110-155k tokens. The next 122 stories are briefed off this same unverified corpus.

HOW: dispatch substrate-cartographer over the 103 file:line citations first - they are mechanically checkable. For each, record VERIFIED / STALE / WRONG with the current file:line. Then the 26 PROVIDED and 33 CONFLICTS tags, which carry the most weight because briefs act on them.

DO NOT rewrite the ACs wholesale. Record the verification result alongside; a wrong tag is a finding for the lead to disposition, not a licence to edit a ratified requirement.

TRAP: some tags cite W&R reference constants (e.g. $CITIZEN_ABLE_SERVE) copied from spec/citizens.md. The real corpus is on disk at ~/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/common/SovietRepublic/media_soviet/buildings_types/ - 1,472 .ini files, $CITIZEN_ABLE_SERVE appears 53 times. Those are checkable too.

title: simulation test binary segfaults under parallel test threads
description:
GATE on evidence reliability. PRE-EXISTING - reproduced on an unmodified tree (1 in 5 runs), NOT introduced by ITER-0000.

SYMPTOM: 'cargo test -p simulation' with default parallel threads segfaults intermittently (SIGSEGV, no Rust backtrace - a raw crash, not a panic). Reproduces ~1-in-3 to 1-in-5.

ROOT CAUSE: crate::init::init() (simulation/src/init.rs:33) pushes into 'static mut' INIT_FUNCS / GSYSTEMS / SAVELOAD_FUNCS with no synchronization. Every TestCtx::new() called it unconditionally, so concurrent test threads race on those pushes. rustc already warns here: 'creating a mutable reference to mutable static ... undefined behavior'.

PARTIAL FIX ALREADY IN TREE: TestCtx::new() now guards the init::init() call with std::sync::Once (simulation/src/tests/mod.rs). This REDUCES but does NOT eliminate the crash - some other unsynchronized global path is also involved and was not chased, to respect the do-not-touch-adjacent-code rule.

WORKAROUND until fixed: run 'cargo test -p simulation -- --test-threads=1'. All ITER-0000 verification used it.

WHY P1: the iterative-development spine treats sentinel scenario runs as evidence. A suite that segfaults 1-in-5 produces a confidently wrong signal - a green run proves little and a red run gets blamed on the wrong change. Fix before the sentinel corpus grows.

TRAP: do not 'fix' this by making the tests single-threaded in CI config and calling it done. That hides the UB rather than removing it; the static mut pattern is the defect.

title: Finish STORY-0149 AC-4: real truck drives dispatch, not a tick countdown
description:
GATE on ITER-0000 meaning anything. economy/market.rs drives delivery off DISPATCH_TRAVEL_TICKS=3, a blind countdown - no vehicle, no road, no distance. 'Nothing teleports' holds as bookkeeping, not physics.

TRAP that has now eaten two agents: trucks are NOT shaped like trains. TrainEnt has no parking, so freight_station.rs can set train.it directly. VehicleEnt carries VehicleState{Parked|Driving|Panicking|RoadToPark} and transportation/road.rs:55-58 moves a vehicle ONLY when Driving/Panicking AND holding a Transporter collider. Setting .it on a parked truck is a NO-OP.

unpark() is transportation/vehicle.rs:107 and needs &mut Simulation, which Market::advance_dispatches (a World+Resources system) lacks. Use the deferred command-buffer pattern from map_dynamic/router.rs:217. There is NO park() counterpart.

Full brief with the next-agent map: docs/superpowers/iterations/brief-truck.md
Prior art: souls/freight_station.rs is the ONLY correct example of driving a dispatched delivery.
Registration was fixed in 35ce342 (the commented block had two bugs: DispatchID::Truck vs SmallTruck, .trans.position vs .trans.pos).

Claude Task tools are main-session-only - a subagent gets 'No matching deferred tools found' regardless of CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS (which is already "1"). br is the only surface every agent can reach. Documented in CLAUDE.md.
